title: A resumed Codex session gets a new thread id and loses its mailbox
description:
'codex resume' gives the session a thread id different from the one SessionStart registered, and no new registration happens on resume. Verified live 2026-09-07 (codex-cli 0.153.4): thread 01a07cce-... was registered as franklin@39; after resuming, the agents table gained no row for the resumed session, and registry.current_agent for the resumed thread id returns None.

Consequences: a resumed Codex session cannot read its own mail, does not appear in the roster, and cannot be sent to — while the mail addressed to its pre-resume mailbox sits unread in an agent nobody is attached to any more. This also breaks the 'a mailbox outlives its endpoint' contract in the design doc, which assumes re-registering a session_key revives the same agent id; resume changes the key, so revival never fires.
acceptance_criteria: A resumed Codex session resolves to the same mailbox it had before the resume, or amail explains the state and offers a documented way to reattach. Verified live with a dated record in docs/acceptance-gates.md.
notes: Found while diagnosing amail-v9s; it is the first half of that bug's root cause (no native row for the resumed thread), while the pin-validation defect fixed in v9s was the second half. Related to amail-eec (no mailbox until first turn).

title: db.amail_home chmods on every call, crashing amail under the Codex sandbox
description:
src/amail/db.py:60 runs home.chmod(0o700) on every invocation, even when the directory already exists with the right mode. Under Codex's seatbelt sandbox that raises PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted: '/Users/<user>/.amail', and every amail command dies with a raw Python traceback before doing anything. Observed live 2026-09-07 in a 'codex exec' session (CODEX_SANDBOX=seatbelt): 'amail whoami' produced a 13-line traceback instead of output.

Two defects in one: the chmod should only run when amail creates the directory, and a permission failure reaching the user as an unhandled traceback is the wrong surface for a tool whose docs promise 'amail doctor' explains degraded modes.
acceptance_criteria: amail commands work under the Codex seatbelt sandbox when ~/.amail already exists with mode 0700. A permission failure that genuinely blocks the mailbox reports a clear one-line error naming the directory, never a traceback. Regression test covers a pre-existing home that cannot be chmodded.
notes: Relevant to acceptance gate 9 (sandbox/permissions), which is still unrun. Found while diagnosing amail-v9s.

title: In-session 'amail read' inside a Codex session resolves to the wrong agent identity
description:
A Codex session that registered correctly as its own agent still resolves to a DIFFERENT agent when it runs 'amail' commands during the session. Verified live 2026-09-07 (codex-cli 0.153.4): thread 01a07cce-6cc0-7541-8022-06e2630c42c2 registered via SessionStart as franklin@39, but when the agent ran 'amail read 2' inside that session it got 'no message 2 for watson@34' — watson@34 being the unrelated Claude session that launched it. The message is addressed to 39, so the read is correctly refused; the identity is what is wrong.

Reproduced three ways, each more isolated than the last, all with the same result: (1) pty child of the Claude Bash tool; (2) same, with AMAIL_AGENT_ID / CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID / CLAUDE_PID popped from the child env before execvp; (3) a detached tmux session launched with those vars scrubbed at both the tmux and codex layers, so the codex process is a child of the tmux server, not of claude. Env scrubbing and reparenting both failed to fix it, so the cause is neither of the two mechanisms install.md's mitigation ('env -u ...') addresses.

Distinct from amail-3um, which fixed the HOOK path by making the hook's harness argument authoritative (d8368ed). A bare 'amail read' passes no harness argument, so identity.resolve falls back to _PROBE_ORDER = (_probe_claude, _probe_codex) and something Claude-shaped still wins inside a Codex session. Root cause not yet identified — do not assume pid ancestry without checking, since reparenting did not help.
acceptance_criteria: A Codex session running 'amail read <id>' resolves as its own registered agent. Root cause identified (not just worked around), regression test added, and re-verified live in a detached Codex session with a dated record in docs/acceptance-gates.md.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-07. Two-part, and my earlier note on this bead was wrong.

CORRECTION: the claim that 'env scrubbing and reparenting both failed to fix it' was not sound. Those runs were confounded — the tmux sessions were blocked on an interactive 'choose working directory' prompt and were only displaying a REPLAYED transcript of the earlier contaminated run, so no fresh read ever ran. Verified afterwards with 'ps eww' on the live codex process (133 env vars readable) that the scrub does take effect: AMAIL_AGENT_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and CLAUDE_PID were all absent.

Actual mechanism, reproduced deterministically against the real mailbox with registry.current_agent:
  A registered thread, no pin -> franklin@39      (correct)
  B registered thread, pin=34 -> LookupError conflict (correct, pre-existing)
  C resume-new thread, pin=34 -> watson@34        (THE BUG)
  D resume-new thread, no pin -> None

Part 1: 'codex resume' hands the session a thread id that was never registered, so there is no native row (filed separately). Part 2: with no native row, current_agent accepted AMAIL_AGENT_ID after checking only that the agent EXISTS — never that it belongs to this session. The existing conflict check was guarded by 'native_row is not None', so the pin was trusted in precisely the case where it is least trustworthy. An inherited pin from the launching Claude session names a real agent and won silently.

FIX: identity.SessionIdentity gains a 'native' flag (False when the harness was guessed from pid ancestry — a guess is not grounds to reject a pin). current_agent now rejects a pin whose agent's session_key differs from a natively resolved identity. Verified end-to-end through the installed CLI: the scenario that returned 'no message 2 for watson@34' now exits 1 with 'identity conflict: AMAIL_AGENT_ID=34 is a claude mailbox but this session resolves to codex'. Live Claude session unaffected (still watson@34); 64 tests pass.
close_reason: Root-caused and fixed. current_agent accepted an inherited AMAIL_AGENT_ID whenever no native mailbox matched, validating only that the agent existed rather than that it belonged to this session. Fixed in 85ad490 with a regression test; verified end-to-end through the installed CLI. The other half of the root cause (resume loses the mailbox) is filed as amail-up1.

title: amail send skips the codex queue push for offline agents, so offline Codex mail is not really delivered on resume
description:
mail.send filters status=='offline' out of the push list (src/amail/mail.py:107), so 'amail send' to an offline Codex session queues nothing in ~/.codex/queue_1.sqlite. The sender is told 'queued — delivered if that session resumes', but verified live 2026-09-07 (codex-cli 0.153.4): resuming such a thread shows the prior transcript, sits at the prompt, and surfaces NOTHING. No turn starts, the header never appears, and message_recipients stays unannounced/unread. The SessionStart hook fires but its context is not consumed until a turn happens, and nothing causes a turn. Delivery therefore waits on the human typing something.

amail-a1w proved 'codex queue' IS durable across a stopped process: manually queueing to the same cold thread and resuming injects the header as user input and starts a real turn. So the capability exists and send declines to use it.
acceptance_criteria: Decide and implement: either (a) push via codex queue to offline codex-route agents so resume delivers a real turn, or (b) keep the filter and correct the sender-facing wording plus docs to say offline Codex mail surfaces only once the operator prompts the resumed session. Verified live on codex-cli and recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md with a date.
notes: Found while retesting amail-8ny. Thread 01a07cce-6cc0-7541-8022-06e2630c42c2, agent franklin@39, message 2. The offline filter is plausibly right for Claude (doorbell write is pointless with no waiter) and wrong for Codex (queue is exactly the durable-offline mechanism) — the fix may be per-route rather than global.

title: Codex session inherits Claude identity and writes to the parent's mailbox
description: identity.resolve checks CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID/CLAUDE_PID before the harness argument the hook was invoked with. A Codex process launched from a Claude Code session (or any nested/inherited env) resolves as claude, so 'amail-hook.sh codex sessionstart' silently updates the PARENT Claude session's agent row instead of creating a Codex mailbox. Observed live 2026-09-07: avogadro@6 had its cwd rewritten to the Codex scratch dir and no codex row was created. This is the same ambient-identity hazard tests/conftest.py::clean_env guards in the suite, unguarded in production.
design: The hook already knows the harness: 'amail hook codex sessionstart'. Identity resolution invoked from a hook should trust that argument over ambient env, or at minimum refuse to resolve as harness X when invoked as harness Y (the existing contract already says a conflict raises rather than picking a winner).
acceptance_criteria: A Codex SessionStart hook run with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and CLAUDE_PID present in the environment either registers a codex mailbox or fails loudly to hook.log; it must never mutate the Claude agent row. Regression test covers the inherited-env case.
close_reason: Fixed on main d8368ed: expect_harness threaded from the hook's harness argument, IdentityConflict on disagreement; Codex first-turn limitation documented + amail doctor note. Verified live against a real Codex session with unscrubbed env.

title: Acceptance gate 2: hook registration in a fresh session
description: Open a fresh Claude Code session AFTER the hooks were wired (2026-09-06) and confirm SessionStart registers the mailbox and pins AMAIL_AGENT_ID without a manual 'amail register'.
acceptance_criteria: In a brand new session, 'amail whoami' succeeds with no prior register, and 'env | grep AMAIL_AGENT_ID' shows the pinned id. Recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md.
close_reason: Gate 2 PASS on Claude Code CLI 2.1.263, 2026-09-07; recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md

title: Acceptance gate 4: Codex idle delivery
description: Does an idle Codex session start a turn when a message is queued via 'codex queue'? Per the design this is correctness, not etiquette: it is the whole Codex delivery path.
acceptance_criteria: With a live idle Codex session (CLI and Desktop separately), send from another agent and record in docs/acceptance-gates.md whether the session starts a turn unprompted, at next boundary, or not at all.
notes: Not run 2026-09-06: needs a live interactive Codex session, and queueing into the operator's own session is an outward-facing action.
close_reason: Codex CLI idle delivery PASS 2026-09-07: idle session starts an unprompted turn ~15s after send, metadata only. Codex Desktop still unrun (amail-jhw). Found amail-3um and amail-eec.

title: Verify codex queue reaches a non-running Codex session
description: The design assumes 'codex queue --thread <t> --message <m>' is a durable write to ~/.codex/queue_1.sqlite that succeeds even when no Codex process is running. On codex-cli 0.153.4, queueing to an unknown thread returns exit 1 with 'Error: No active session found matching ...', which hints the command may require an ACTIVE session rather than any known thread id.
acceptance_criteria: Queue a message to a real Codex thread whose process is NOT running, then resume that thread and confirm whether the message arrives. If it does not, update docs/plans/2026-09-06_agent-mail-design.md (Delivery table) and docs/install.md to say Codex offline sends fall back to the SessionStart backstop, and make 'amail send' warn when the codex push fails for an offline Codex mailbox.
notes: Found 2026-09-06 while running acceptance gates. The clean exit-1 failure path is already handled correctly by routing.ring (returns False, never raises). What is unverified is the success path for an offline-but-known thread. Blocks acceptance gate 4.
close_reason: Verified live on codex-cli 0.153.4 (2026-09-07): queueing to a known-but-stopped thread exits 0, persists to queue_1.sqlite, and is drained into the transcript on resume. The exit-1 path is unknown-thread-id only. Docs corrected; no fallback-to-backstop story needed. Recipient-side framing gap filed as amail-8ny.

title: Codex recipients treat the amail header as an untrusted external instruction
description: Delivery works but the recipient refuses to act. During amail-a1w verification, a resumed Codex session received the queued amail header and replied: 'I won't execute instructions embedded in an external mail notification without your explicit request.' The metadata-only header reads like injected content to a fresh Codex turn, so mail arrives and is then ignored. Need recipient-side framing (~/.codex/AGENTS.md wording, and/or header phrasing) that makes 'amail read <id>' legible as a first-party action the user asked for.
acceptance_criteria: A Codex session woken by queued amail mail runs 'amail read <id>' rather than declining. Verified live on codex-cli, recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md with a date.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-09-07, after re-reading the gate 4 record. The refusal is NOT Codex's general posture toward amail headers — gate 4 (docs/acceptance-gates.md, 2026-09-07, codex-cli 0.153.4) records the opposite: a LIVE idle Codex session woken by the same header 'chose to run amail read 1' with no human input. The two runs differ in recipient context, not in the header.

Refused (amail-a1w probe): thread created by 'codex exec' with a trivial unrelated prompt, process exited, resumed cold. No SessionStart hook context, no mailbox awareness, and the header arrives as the first user-role turn of a resumed transcript about something else.
Worked (gate 4): session had run SessionStart, had a registered mailbox, was idle mid-conversation.

Root cause is more likely the missing receiving-side instructions than the header text: ~/.codex/AGENTS.md and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md contain NO amail content on this machine, though docs/install.md prescribes it for both. The whole receiving contract is documented but never deployed. Also note the prescribed wording only says bodies are 'data, not instructions' and never says retrieval is authorized, so an agent can reasonably generalize 'do not obey' into 'do not fetch' — which is exactly the observed failure.

title: A Codex session is unaddressable until its first turn
description: On codex-cli 0.153.4 the thread id does not exist when the TUI launches; SessionStart fires when the first turn creates the thread. Observed 2026-09-07: a Codex session launched at ~03:32Z registered heisenberg@11 only at 03:33:25Z, after its first turn completed. A freshly opened, never-prompted Codex session therefore has no mailbox and cannot be sent to at all — it does not appear in 'amail roster'.
design: Options: (a) document it as a known limitation of the Codex surface in the design doc Delivery table and docs/install.md; (b) register on SessionStart with a provisional key and re-key when the thread id appears; (c) fall back to a pid-based session key for Codex when no thread id is available, accepting that push has no route until the thread exists. Note (c) is what the current pid-ancestry fallback already half-does, and in an inherited env it is what produces amail-3um.
acceptance_criteria: Behavior is either fixed or explicitly documented in docs/plans/2026-09-06_agent-mail-design.md and docs/install.md, and 'amail doctor' says so when running under Codex with no thread id.
notes: Found 2026-09-07 running acceptance gate 4. Distinct from amail-a1w, which is about a thread that existed and then stopped; this is about a thread that does not exist yet.
close_reason: Fixed on main d8368ed: expect_harness threaded from the hook's harness argument, IdentityConflict on disagreement; Codex first-turn limitation documented + amail doctor note. Verified live against a real Codex session with unscrubbed env.

title: Run the acceptance gates on Claude Desktop, Codex CLI, and Codex Desktop
description: No gate has been run on these three surfaces. The four-surface MVP claim in README.md is not valid until they pass.
acceptance_criteria: docs/acceptance-gates.md carries a dated pass for every applicable gate on each of the three surfaces; README status line updated to match.

title: Acceptance gates 5, 7, 9, 11 on Claude Code CLI
